name: Hiram Page
role: Book of Mormon witness who claimed revelations through a stone
dateNote: He was one of the Eight Witnesses in June 1829 and was baptized on 11 April 1830; section 28 dates from September 1830.
importance: In 1830 he said he received revelations for the Church through a stone, and some members accepted them. Section 28 tells Oliver Cowdery to tell him privately that those writings were not from the Lord. He later renounced the writings after that revelation. He later moved with the Saints to Ohio and Missouri and left the Church in 1838.
connections: He married Catherine Whitmer in 1825, so the Whitmer brothers were his brothers-in-law. Section 28 sends Oliver Cowdery to speak with him.

sources.title: Hiram Page, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 1800, Vermont; physician and farmer; baptized 11 Apr. 1830; later in Kirtland, Jackson and Clay Counties, Far West; left the Church 1838; briefly joined McLellin’s church in 1848. Death date shown only as a fragment (12 Aug. 1852) near Excelsior Springs, Missouri. JSP notes he denounced the revelations in response to Joseph Smith’s revelation.
